headline: CEC at 84.5% counted -- Netanyahu bloc 54, Eisenkot bloc 49, Arab parties 17
dek: With 84.5% of ballot boxes counted as of 12:34 p.m. Israel time, the CEC gives Netanyahu's bloc 54 seats, Eisenkot's Yashar-led bloc 49, and the Arab-led parties (Joint List 11 + Ra'am 6) 17.
sources: Israel Central Elections Committee, via Times of Israel liveblog
fault_line: Should the change bloc govern with the Arab parties (66 seats on this count) despite Netanyahu's 'shame/danger' framing, or is an Arab-backed government illegitimate?

sections.what_happened: With 84.5% of ballot boxes counted as of 12:34 p.m. Israel time, the CEC gives Netanyahu's bloc 54 seats, Eisenkot's Yashar-led bloc 49, and the Arab-led parties (Joint List 11 + Ra'am 6) 17. Likud 27, Yashar 22. Below threshold: Reservists 2.7%, People of Israel 1.6%, Charedi Public 0.2%. This SUPERSEDES the 76.8% / 54-47-19 partial in totw-20261028-1400-01: Eisenkot +2, Arab parties -2, Netanyahu unchanged at 54, still 7 short of 61. Double-envelope ballots (soldiers etc., ~600,000 per Daily Letter) are counted later (Oct 29 per Petek timeline); official results Nov 4. The 1500-04 monitor ('no advance past 76.8% retrieved in-window') is now corrected by this catch-up: the advance landed at 14:34-14:39 but surfaced only after that scan's search pass.
sections.what_verified: Count figures: primary-source single family -- the CEC itself (T1 official/primary data). Times of Israel (T3) is the carrier of the same CEC data, not an independent corroboration; The Petek (no declared tier) independently applies Bader-Ofer to CEC vote counts (4,400,507 valid votes, 10,156 stations) and matches 54/49/17, but as an undeclared-tier source it does NOT count toward corroboration. The Times (London) liveblog independently reports the same 84.5% / 54-49-17 balance.
sections.what_disputed: (1) A 56/48/16 balance circulates (Times of Israel Golan-entry footer; Monoscoops aggregator, 'nearly 3.5 million votes counted') with NO timestamp tying it to a CEC release -- NOT adopted; the timestamped CEC figure is 54/49/17 at 84.5%. (2) Petek's own timeline step '~08:00 About 90% counted' conflicts with 84.5% at 12:34 -- the timestamped figure governs; the timeline step is treated as stale/approximate. (3) Golan's '65' arithmetic (49+16) was computed on an earlier partial; on 54/49/17 the change bloc + Arab parties = 66, but no coalition agreement exists -- arithmetic is not an agreement.
sections.why_matters: The count moved -- Netanyahu did NOT gain: Eisenkot +2, Arab parties -2, and the kingmaker math now runs through 17 Arab seats. Hard number in title: '54-49-17'.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (landed 14:34-14:39 , inside the prior window, missed by the 1500 scan) + NEWEST COUNT -- Israel election: CEC at 84.5% counted -- Netanyahu bloc 54, Eisenkot bloc 49, Arab parties 17; Netanyahu still 7 short of 61

totw_analysis: Our read: The count moved -- Netanyahu did NOT gain: Eisenkot +2, Arab parties -2, and the kingmaker math now runs through 17 Arab seats. Hard number in title: '54-49-17'. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should the change bloc govern with the Arab parties (66 seats on this count) despite Netanyahu's 'shame/danger' framing, or is an Arab-backed government illegitimate?
